headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is elevated by mixed data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard, and MCP outputs by default; oh-my-openagent injects runtime MCPs/hooks and touches AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through shared files or copied content, even though direct pairwise documentation is absent.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or copied clipboard content
IF either agent treats file contents or AGENTS.md as instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents
Separate workspaces per agent
Add a prompt-injection filter for file and README content
Require explicit provenance tags before executing instructions from files
requires-engineering: add MCP provenance and allowlist enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers/MCP servers; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data with broad egress. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive code or auth material can flow to external services without strong isolation.
conditions: IF the two agents share project files, clipboard, or the same authenticated workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents or session history to external providers
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Remove shared clipboard access during concurrent use
Restrict network egress to approved endpoints
Rotate any exposed provider auth data
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; oh-my-openagent can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks. Both can act on the same mutable project state, so concurrent edits or git changes can race and corrupt work unless externally serialized.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or filesystem tree
IF either agent modifies git state or generated files without locking
mitigations: Run only one agent per repo at a time
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Enable file locking or a task queue
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can produce code or actions from open files, and oh-my-openagent exposes tasking and message tools plus runtime hooks. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code changes, browser actions, or team messages.
conditions: IF Cursor outputs code or instructions that oh-my-openagent consumes as authoritative
IF oh-my-openagent uses those outputs to create tasks, messages, or edits without review
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require tests or lint checks before downstream action
Limit downstream agent permissions to read-only until verified
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents; oh-my-openagent is open-source but also handles project code, session history, and provider auth data. The pair can therefore mix sensitive code and credentials across different retention and logging regimes, creating a compliance mismatch even without a documented residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential code is processed in either agent
IF their logging or retention settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to both agents
Align retention settings before use
Disable verbose session logging
Document data-flow boundaries for each agent
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and retention review
